correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction: the prime-power identity is inclusion-exclusion of multiples of p; Faulhaber supplies exact polynomial coefficients; lowest powers are 1 (even m) and 2 (odd m), with nonzero Bernoulli coefficients; choosing p>k+2 outside two finite Bernoulli numerator prime sets makes pH_m Eisenstein for m=s,k over Z_(p). The valuation-one constant and unit leading term yield irreducibility. If numerical integer divisibility held for every prime power, polynomial long division and vanishing of a smaller-degree rational remainder prove divisibility over Q. Two irreducible H_m cannot divide each other unless associates; degree comparison or, at consecutive even/odd indices, inconsistent coefficient ratios exclude associates. Thus all integers s>=2 and k>s are covered. The standard-library exact checker replays 38 integer identities, 19 Eisenstein profiles, and 171 distinct-moment polynomial divisions; the finite experiment is not the proof.

value.rationale: The precise universally quantified divisibility sets were introduced by the focal primary paper, which proved only finiteness. This gives the first natural complete all-higher-moments classification, an infinite improvement from qualitative finiteness to singleton structure. The argument identifies a reusable obstruction: prime-power Faulhaber factors that are irreducible at a suitable p and cannot divide one another. It is not a routine numerical table, arbitrary slice, or isolated small example; its exception s=1 is understood separately in subsequent literature.
